item.description:
Trump claims his backing of Netanyahu reversed his 'decisive defeat' in Israeli elections

US President Donald Trump has claimed that his endorsement reversed Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu's possible "defeat".

"When President Trump endorsed Bibi Netanyahu, the whole tide turned, and now, rather than a decisive defeat for a Great Prime Minister, it looks like a big come-from-behind stalemate, or even a WIN for Netanyahu," he wrote on  his social media platform Truth Social.

"It all took place AFTER the Endorsement by President Trump, who only wants what is good for the Middle East, Israel, and the United States of America!"

item.title: Coalition with Arab parties would be ‘a shame and a disgrace’, Netanyahu says
item.description:
Coalition with Arab parties would be ‘a shame and a disgrace’, Netanyahu says

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said a coalition with Arab parties to form a government would be “a shame and a disgrace".

"It is forbidden - simply forbidden - to endanger Israel and to establish a government that relies on anti-Zionist Arab parties," he told crowds. 

He also said that Israel should not rely on Arab parties, which he described as being "opposed to our very existence".

item.title: Netanyahu's bloc down to 57 seats, as 42 percent of ballots counted
item.description:
Netanyahu's bloc down to 57 seats, as 42 percent of ballots counted

Data from the Central Elections Committee indicates that over 2.1 million ballots have been counted, nearly 42%.

Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc remains in the lead, but has gone down to 57 seats. Eisenkot’s bloc follows in at 47 seats, while Palestinian-led parties hold 16 seats.

item.title: UN commission reports more than 1,000 Palestinians killed in West Bank since October 2023
item.description: The UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and Israel said Tuesday that Israeli forces had killed 1,080 Palestinians in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, between Oct. 7, 2023, and Sept. 30, Anadolu reports. Presenting the findings during a hybrid briefing, with all three members participating virtually, Srinivasan Muralidhar of India said the commission documented the deaths and thousands of injuries during the period. Muralidhar said the fatalities included at least 784 men, 237 boys, 22 women and seven girls. He said 10,009 Palestinians had also been injured by Israeli forces in the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem. item.title: UN urges protection of civilians after Jordanian airstrikes in southern Syria
item.description: The UN on Tuesday called for the protection of civilians and respect for Syria’s sovereignty following Jordanian airstrikes in southern Syria, Anadolu reports. Spokeswoman Daniela Gross De Almeida told reporters that the UN is “closely” monitoring developments and had taken note of statements issued by both Jordanian and Syrian authorities on the operation and its circumstances. “The Secretary-General (Antonio Guterres) condemns any loss of civilian lives, and we underscore the obligation of all parties to take all precautions to protect civilians in line with international law,” said De Almeida. She added that the UN supports efforts by the parties to establish the facts surrounding the incident, while emphasizing the importance of respecting the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of […]

item.title: The Mecca Pact Courts Iran: Containment Comes Full Circle
item.description: For nearly half a century, Iran’s adversaries have tried to isolate it, intimidate it, sanction it into submission and bomb it into irrelevance. Now, in a remarkable inversion of regional power politics, three countries historically invested in its containment have arrived in Tehran to discuss their security with the very state they were supposed to marginalise. The country they could not defeat is becoming the country they cannot afford to ignore. Yesterday, Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, Pakistan’s army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalın met Iranian officials in an encounter whose diplomatic courtesies barely concealed its strategic significance. The Mecca Pact, the joint defence agreement that Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan signed […]

item.title: Whose interests does the ceasefire serve?
item.description: A new report released yesterday by the UN Commission of Inquiry states that Israel is still committing genocide in Gaza after the ceasefire agreement which was reached on 10 October 2025.
